name: Harvest Hill
award: 2024 Federal 4% and noncompetitive state housing tax credits
headline: Ulysses Development Group is building Harvest Hill, 152 new one- to three-bedroom apartments for households at 30% to 70% AMI at 11801 Wadsworth Blvd. in Broomfield, a quarter mile from RTD's Broomfield Station. It won a 2024-cycle federal 4% credit plus $800,000 of noncompetitive state credit from CHFA, with $31.5M of CHFA bonds.
why_it_matters: A transit-oriented 4% bond deal that closed by stacking CHFA bonds and credits with city money, DOLA HOME funds and Section 811 vouchers, state More Housing Now and Colorado Clean Energy Fund money; it is now pre-leasing for November 2026 move-ins.

status.label: Financing closed (April 2025), under construction; pre-leasing for November 2026 move-ins
status.detail: Mile High CRE reported the construction and permanent financing closing on 2025-04-14 and the groundbreaking on 2025-06-17; the architect reported framing in progress in November 2025, and the management company's site was pre-leasing for November 2026 move-ins as of 2026-10-21. Completion or a certificate of occupancy is not confirmed by a public record.

next_step: Watch for a certificate of occupancy and first move-ins (November 2026 targeted by the leasing site; spring 2027 in the 2025 financing reports).

key_numbers.meaning: 48 one-, 68 two- and 36 three-bedroom units; 8 at 30%, 11 at 50%, 101 at 60% and 32 at 70% AMI (averaging about 60% AMI, computed).

key_numbers.value: $2,182,105 a year in federal 4% credit, plus $800,000 state credit
key_numbers.meaning: Federal credit runs 10 years; amounts are marked subject to change. News reports put the credits at about $20M federal and $4.8M state.
CHFA is the bond issuer; U.S. Bank provided about $42M of construction loans and the tax credit equity.
Total financing reported at closing in April 2025.

facts.value: Family, new construction; not in a QCT, DDA or SADDA; Section 8 column marked No
5.77 acres, about 26 units per acre; four-story center-hall building of about 160,000 sq ft; 255 parking spaces; average unit about 867 sq ft (units 624 to 1,161 sq ft)
About a quarter mile from RTD's Broomfield Station on US 36

About 3,500 sq ft of shared space (clubroom, work-from-home lounge, children's playroom), two courtyards, playground, indoor storage for over 75 bikes, solar panels for common-area power; NGBS certification targeted
Eight Section 811 vouchers from DOLA for people who are or are at risk of being homeless

facts.item: Starting rents (leasing site, with a one-month-free concession annualized)

Reported as $4.8M of accelerated state credits (consistent with $800,000 a year over six years, inferred).

background.text: In February 2023 BizWest reported that Ulysses Development Group planned a 52-apartment workforce project called Harvest Station, for households up to 80% AMI, at the northwest corner of Wadsworth Boulevard and 118th Avenue, with a PUD amendment, final plat and site development plan before Broomfield's Land Use Review Committee. This is inferred to be an earlier version of the Harvest Hill site, given the same developer and corner; the outcome of that review was not found.

Ulysses closed construction and permanent financing in April 2025, with groundbreaking then set for 2025-06-11; the ceremony was held on 2025-06-17 with Broomfield's mayor, state legislators and DOLA and CHFA staff.
The architect reported that construction, led by Taylor Kohrs, began in May 2025 and that framing was in progress by November 2025.
The groundbreaking coverage cites Broomfield's 2025 housing strategy finding that 62% of households are cost-burdened.
No public document found shows the deal in CHFA's 2024 competitive rounds (Round One applicants, Round Two applicants or awards).

discrepancies.text: Mile High CRE reports a $2M contribution from the City and County of Broomfield, while The Real Deal reports $4M.
The 2025 financing reports target completion in spring 2027, while the developer's project page says end of 2026 and the leasing site offers November 2026 move-ins.
